sources.citation: Righini M, Van Es J, Den Exter PL, et al. Age-adjusted D-dimer cutoff levels to rule out pulmonary embolism: the ADJUST-PE study. JAMA. 2014;311(11):1117-24.
sources.population_setting: 3346 consecutive ED outpatients with suspected PE, 19 centres in Belgium, France, Netherlands, Switzerland, 2010-2013
sources.correction_check: PubMed search of PMID with retracted publication[pt] OR erratum: none found (2026-09-25). Scite not used.
sources.quality_note: Single-arm management study (no randomised comparator); failure rate CI 0.1-1.7%. Assay: highly sensitive D-dimer, cut-offs in ug/L.

sources.citation: O'Hare AM, Choi AI, Bertenthal D, et al. Age affects outcomes in chronic kidney disease. J Am Soc Nephrol. 2007;18(10):2758-65.
sources.population_setting: 209,622 US veterans with CKD stages 3-5 (eGFR <60), mean follow-up 3.2 years
sources.correction_check: PubMed search of PMID with retracted publication[pt] OR erratum: none found (2026-09-25).
sources.quality_note: Veterans cohort, predominantly men; outcome is treated ESRD vs all-cause death; stage-3-specific figures for 85+ not in abstract.

sources.citation: Hallan SI, Matsushita K, Sang Y, et al. Age and association of kidney measures with mortality and end-stage renal disease. JAMA. 2012;308(22):2349-60.
sources.population_setting: 2,051,244 participants, 46 cohorts, multiple continents, mean follow-up 5.8 years
sources.correction_check: Not specifically searched for erratum; no notice shown in PubMed record.
sources.quality_note: Large, high-quality; supports albuminuria adding risk information at all ages.

sources.citation: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) CKD Work Group. KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease. Kidney Int. 2024;105(4S):S117-S314.
sources.tool_used: PubMed search (record only; no abstract, text not opened)
sources.quality_note: Located but text NOT opened; cannot support wording yet.

claims.claim: ADJUST-PE: age x 10 cut-off (age 50+) after clinical probability score; 3-month failure 1 of 331 below the age-adjusted cut-off.
claims.supporting_passage: All consecutive outpatients who presented to the emergency department with clinically suspected PE were assessed by a sequential diagnostic strategy based on the clinical probability assessed using either the simplified, revised Geneva score or the 2-level Wells score for PE; highly sensitive D-dimer measurement; and computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA). ... The 3-month failure rate in patients with a D-dimer level higher than 500 µg/L but below the age-adjusted cutoff was 1 of 331 patients (0.3% [95% CI, 0.1%-1.7%]).
claims.pico_timeframe: ED outpatients with suspected PE and non-high/unlikely clinical probability; age-adjusted vs 500 ug/L cut-off; adjudicated VTE at 3 months
claims.safe_wording: In a 2014 European study of 3346 emergency patients with suspected PE, people aged 50 or over whose clinical score was not high used a cut-off of age x 10 µg/L; of 331 followed without a scan, 1 had a clot within 3 months.
claims.qualifications: Only after a non-high/unlikely clinical probability score; units µg/L (assay-dependent, FEU not stated in abstract); no randomised comparator.

numbers.meaning: 3-month failure among those between 500 and age-adjusted cut-off, untreated

claims.claim: Among 673 people 75+ with non-high probability, scan-free exclusion rose from 6.4% to 29.7% without additional false negatives.
claims.supporting_passage: Among the 766 patients 75 years or older, of whom 673 had a nonhigh clinical probability, using the age-adjusted cutoff instead of the 500 µg/L cutoff increased the proportion of patients in whom PE could be excluded on the basis of D-dimer from 43 of 673 patients (6.4% [95% CI, 4.8%-8.5%) to 200 of 673 patients (29.7% [95% CI, 26.4%-33.3%), without any additional false-negative findings.
claims.pico_timeframe: Age 75+, non-high clinical probability; age-adjusted vs 500 ug/L; 3 months
claims.safe_wording: Among 673 people aged 75 or over whose clinical score was not high, a clot could be ruled out without a scan in about 6 in 100 with the standard cut-off and about 30 in 100 with the age-adjusted cut-off, with no extra missed clots found in that group.
claims.qualifications: Subgroup of 75+ with non-high probability only; 'no additional false negatives' applies to this group.

claims.claim: NICE NG158 advises considering age-adjusted D-dimer for people over 50.
claims.safe_wording: Do not state what UK guidance says; not opened.
claims.qualifications: NICE pages cannot be opened here.

claims.claim: In US veterans with CKD 3-5, older patients had higher death and lower ESRD rates at comparable eGFR; at 85+ death risk always exceeded ESRD risk.
claims.supporting_passage: among those with comparable levels of eGFR, older patients had higher rates of death and lower rates of ESRD than younger patients. ... Among those 85 years or older, the risk of death always exceeded the risk of ESRD in this cohort.
claims.pico_timeframe: 209,622 US veterans, CKD stages 3-5; death (all causes) vs treated ESRD; mean 3.2 years
claims.safe_wording: In a 2007 study of over 200,000 US veterans (mostly men) with reduced kidney function, people aged 85 or over were more likely to die than to reach kidney failure needing dialysis, at every level of kidney function studied.
claims.qualifications: All-cause death, not 'other causes'; stages 3-5 combined; US veterans; observational; follow-up ~3 years.
claims.conflicting_or_uncertain: Hallan 2012 shows low eGFR and albuminuria still carry higher absolute death risk at older ages, so the label is not meaningless.

claims.claim: Urine albumin adds risk information alongside eGFR at all ages.
claims.supporting_passage: Both low eGFR and high albuminuria were independently associated with mortality and ESRD regardless of age across a wide range of populations.
claims.pico_timeframe: 2.05 million people, 46 cohorts; eGFR and ACR vs death and ESRD; mean 5.8 years
claims.safe_wording: Across large studies of people of all ages, both lower kidney function on the blood test and more albumin in the urine were linked with higher risk, so the urine test adds useful information.
claims.qualifications: Association; does not directly show that normal albumin means low kidney-failure risk.

claims.claim: KDIGO/NICE grade CKD by eGFR and albuminuria; NICE recommends ACR; some medicines need dose adjustment.
claims.safe_wording: Not verified; guideline text not opened. Dose-adjustment point may rely on C06-19 evidence if it exists.

candidates.reason: ADJUST-PE abstract supports all study numbers and conditions; NICE claim unverified so omit UK-guidance statement.
O'Hare and Hallan support the core finding and the value of the urine test; KDIGO/NICE wording and medicine-dosing question not verified; 'other causes' wrong.
candidates.revised_angle: Say 'more likely to die than to reach kidney failure needing dialysis' (2007, US veterans, mostly men, stages 3-5); ask about stability and urine albumin; drop or separately source the medicines and guideline claims.
